The meaning of ﴿حَتّى نَعْلَمَ المُجاهِدِينَ﴾ is: that We know them as strivers, whose striving has come into existence, and whose reward is connected to what they have earned (?) — and that their "mask" (maskuhum) on which their reward depends. ("Those who disbelieved") refers to some people of the Children of Israel. The "clarity of their guidance" means their recognition of the Messenger from the Torah. Or they are hypocrites, as if faith had entered their hearts and then they became hypocrites. "Those who were fed" are the people of Badr's provisions. "Guidance became clear" means its existence with the one who calls to it, or it is widespread in every disbeliever. "Guidance became clear" from the standpoint of what it was in itself: these are opinions.

﴿And He will make their deeds fruitless﴾: that is, the deeds by which they hoped for benefit, and "their deeds" by which they plotted against the Messenger and the religion of Islam.

(O you who believe): It was said that it was revealed about the Children of Israel, who embraced Islam and said to the Messenger of Allah: "We have preferred you and come to you with our souls and our families," as if they were conferring a favour by this. So this verse was revealed about them. And His saying: ﴿They consider it a favour to you that they have embraced Islam﴾ [al-Hujurat 17]. From him also: by associating partners with Allah and hypocrisy. From Hudhayfah: by major sins. It was said: by self-admiration (ʿujb), for it consumes good deeds as fire consumes firewood. From Muqatil: by your disobedience to the Messenger. It was also said: "your deeds" means your charities accompanied by reproach and harm.

(And died while they were disbelievers): It is general regarding what necessitates the absence of forgiveness, which is their death upon disbelief. It was said: they are the people of the well (ahl al-qalīb). It was said: it was revealed on account of ʿAdi ibn Hatim, may Allah be pleased with him, who asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about his father. He said: "He had acts of righteousness; so what is his state?" He said: "In the Fire." ʿAdi wept and turned away, and [the Prophet] called him back and said to him: "My father and your father and the father of Ibrahim, the Friend of the Most Merciful, are in the Fire." Then this was revealed.

Al-Sulami read it with a shaddah on the dāl, meaning "that you become weak" (tafturū). The majority read ﴿إلى السَّلْمِ﴾ with a fatḥah on the sīn, while al-Hasan, Abu Rajaʾ, al-Aʿmash, ʿIsa, Talhah, Hamzah and Abu Bakr read it with a kasrah. Al-Zamakhshari said: It has been read: "wa-la tadʿū", from "idda'a al-qawm" and "tada'aw" when they claim (idda'aw), like your saying: "irtamaw al-ṣayd" and "taramaw" (they shot at the game). ﴿And He will not deprive you﴾: Ibn ʿAbbas said: "He will not wrong you." It was said: "He will not strip you of the reward of your deeds." It was said: "He will not diminish you." Al-Zamakhshari said, and Abu ʿUbayd said: "lan yatirakum" is from "watarta al-rajul", when you kill a slain person for him from a son, a brother, a close relative or kinsman. He said: or you take his wealth. He said: or his property. Its reality is that you make him single out from his relative or his wealth, from "al-watr", which is "the single" (al-fard). So the waste of the doer's work and the nullifying of its reward is compared to the "watr" of the one who takes the blood-revenge, and this is among eloquent speech. From it is the saying of the Prophet, upon him be prayer and peace: "Whoever misses the ʿAsr prayer, it is as if he has been robbed of his family and his property," meaning that he was singled out from them by killing and plunder.

﴿The life of this world is but play and amusement﴾: This is a belittling of the effect of this world, that is, "so do not weaken (p-86) in jihad." He informed about it with that, with regard to what is specific to it of such things. As for what is in it of obedience and the affairs of the Hereafter, it is not included in that.

﴿He will give you your rewards﴾: that is, the reward of your deeds of faith and piety. ﴿And will not ask of you your wealth﴾. Sufyan ibn ʿUyaynah said: that is, much of your wealth; He only asks you for a quarter of a tenth, so be generous of your souls. It was said: there is no need for it, rather He returns the reward of your spending to you. It was said: He only asks you for His wealth, because He is the true owner of it, and He is the Bestower by giving it. It was said: the pronoun in "yas'alukum" refers to the Messenger, meaning He does not ask you for a wage for conveying the message, as He said: ﴿Say: I do not ask you for any reward for it, and I am not of those who impose themselves﴾ [Sad 86].

(If He should ask it of you all and press you): that is, he insists in urging.

﴿You would be stingy and He would bring forth your resentments﴾: that is, you would revile the Messenger, your hearts would be constricted likewise, and you would conceal a grudge that would take your wealth. The majority read ﴿ويُخْرِجْ أضْغانَكُمْ﴾ in the jussive, as the answer to the condition, and the verb is attributed to Allah, or to the Messenger, or to stinginess. ʿAbd al-Warith, from Abu ʿAmr, read "wa-yukhriju" with a raf (nominative) as a resumptive sentence, meaning "and He brings forth." Abu Hatim related it from ʿIsa. In al-Lawamih, from ʿAbd al-Warith, from Abu ʿAmr: "wa-takhruju" with a tāʾ and a fatḥah on it, with a ḍammah on the rāʾ and the jīm, and "aḍghānukum" in the nominative, meaning "and it comes out" or "your resentments will come out," with the raf governed by its verb. This is what was feared would befall the believers, and it is what Muhammad ibn Maslamah drew near to Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf with, and by it he reached his killing, when he said to him: "This man has burdened us and demanded wealth from us."

(There you are, these are the ones): He repeated "ha" as an emphatic exclamation of attention. This construction was discussed earlier in surah Al ʿImran. Al-Zamakhshari said: "Haʾulaʾ" is a relative pronoun (mawṣūl) in the sense of "alladhīna," whose relative clause is "tud'awna," meaning "you are those who are called," or "you, O addressees, are these described ones." (In the way of Allah): it was said: for fighting, and it was said: the zakat, and the wording is more general.

﴿And among you are some who are stingy﴾: that is, with charity and what Allah has made obligatory upon him. ﴿And whoever is stingy is only stingy against himself﴾: that is, his harm does not pass to others. The verb "bakhila" is transitive with "ʿalā" and with "ʿan." It is said: "bakhiltu ʿalayhi" and "ʿanhu," and "ṣallaytu ʿalayhi" and "ʿanhu." It seems that when they are transitive with "ʿan," they imply the meaning of withholding, as if it were said: "I withheld from him by stinginess."

﴿And Allah is the Free of need and you are the needy﴾: that is, the Free of need absolutely, since needs are impossible for Him. And you are the needy absolutely, due to your need for what you require in this world and for the reward in the Hereafter. (And if you turn away): it is a conjunction on "(and if you believe and fear Allah)," that is, "and if you turn away," that is, from faith and piety.

﴿He will replace you with another people﴾: that is, He will create a people other than you who are eager for faith and piety, not turning away from them, as He said: "and bring a new creation." The identification of those people, and that they are the Ansar, or the Successors (al-Tabiʿun), or the people of Yemen, or Kindah and al-Nakhaʿ, or the non-Arabs, or Persia and the Romans, or the angels, are opinions. The address is to the Quraysh, or to the people of Madinah, are two views. Abu Hurayrah related that "he, upon him be prayer and peace, was asked about this, and Salman was at his side, so he placed his hand on his thigh and said: 'This one and his people; by Him in whose hand is my soul, if faith were suspended at the Pleiades, men from Persia would reach it.'" If this hadith is authentic, then it is necessary to refer the identification of what is left vague in His saying ("another people") to the identification by the Messenger.

﴿Then they will not be like you﴾: that is, in opposition, turning away, and stinginess.

(And if you turn away): it is a conjunction on "(and if you believe and fear Allah)," that is, "and if you turn away," that is, from faith and piety.

And whoever is stingy is only stingy against himself. And Allah is the Free of need, and you are the needy. In these two sentences there is nearness (taqrīb) (p-85) to their notoriety, but He did not specify them by name, out of sparing them and their relatives, and being content with what they displayed of following the Law, even if they concealed the opposite of it.

﴿And you will surely recognize them by the tone of their speech﴾: They used to agree among themselves on expressions that they addressed to the Messenger, whose outward meaning was good while they meant something ugly by them. They also would utter speech that suggested following [the Messenger], while they were contrary to that, like their saying at the time of victory: ﴿Indeed, we were with you﴾ [al-ʿAnkabūt 10], and other such things, like their saying: ﴿If we return to Madinah﴾ [al-Munafiqun 8], and His saying: ﴿Indeed, our houses are exposed﴾ [al-Ahzab 13]. The apparent meaning of "showing" and "recognizing by marks" is the existence of recognition in the future through the tone of speech. The lam in ﴿ولَتَعْرِفَنَّهم﴾ ("and you will surely recognize them") is the lam of the answer to an implied oath (lām jawāb al-qasam al-maḥdhūf).

﴿And Allah knows your deeds﴾: This is a general address that includes the believer and the disbeliever. It has been said that it is addressed to the believers only.

The majority (al-Jumhur) read ﴿ولَنَبْلُوَنَّكم حَتّى نَعْلَمَ المُجاهِدِينَ مِنكُمْ﴾ and ﴿ونَبْلُوَ﴾ with the nūn and the wāw. Abu Bakr read them with the yā' in all of these places. Uways read ﴿ونَبْلَوْا﴾ with a sukūn on the wāw and with the nūn. Al-A'mash read them with a sukūn on it and with the yā'. This is by way of independent sentences (qaṭʿ), to inform that His testing is continuous. The meaning of ﴿حَتّى نَعْلَمَ المُجاهِدِينَ﴾ is: that We know them as strivers, whose striving has come into existence, and whose reward is connected to what they have earned (?) — and that their "mask" (maskuhum) on which their reward depends. Or they are hypocrites, as if faith had entered their hearts and then they became hypocrites. "Those who were fed" are the people of Badr's provisions. "Guidance became clear" means its existence with the one who calls to it, or it is widespread in every disbeliever. "Guidance became clear" from the standpoint of what it was in itself: these are opinions.

﴿And He will make their deeds fruitless﴾: that is, the deeds by which they hoped for benefit, and "their deeds" by which they plotted against the Messenger and the religion of Islam.

(O you who believe): It was said that it was revealed about the Children of Israel, who embraced Islam and said to the Messenger of Allah: "We have preferred you and come to you with our souls and our families," as if they were conferring a favour by this. So this verse was revealed about them. And His saying: ﴿They consider it a favour to you that they have embraced Islam﴾ [al-Hujurat 17]. On this view, ﴿ولا تُبْطِلُوا أعْمالَكُمْ﴾ ("do not nullify your deeds") means by conferring favour through Islam. From Ibn ʿAbbas: by showing off and seeking reputation. From him also: by associating partners with Allah and hypocrisy. From Hudhayfah: by major sins. It was said: by self-admiration (ʿujb), for it consumes good deeds as fire consumes firewood. From Muqatil: by your disobedience to the Messenger. It was also said: "your deeds" means your charities accompanied by reproach and harm.

(And died while they were disbelievers): It is general regarding what necessitates the absence of forgiveness, which is their death upon disbelief. It was said: they are the people of the well (ahl al-qalīb). It was said: it was revealed on account of ʿAdi ibn Hatim, may Allah be pleased with him, who asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about his father. He said: "He had acts of righteousness; so what is his state?" He said: "In the Fire." ʿAdi wept and turned away, and [the Prophet] called him back and said to him: "My father and your father and the father of Ibrahim, the Friend of the Most Merciful, are in the Fire." Then this was revealed.

﴿So do not weaken and call to peace﴾: and it is reconciliation (ṣulḥ). The majority read ﴿وتَدْعُوا﴾ as the present tense of "daʿā". Al-Sulami read it with a shaddah on the dāl, meaning "that you become weak" (tafturū). The majority read ﴿إلى السَّلْمِ﴾ with a fatḥah on the sīn, while al-Hasan, Abu Rajaʾ, al-Aʿmash, ʿIsa, Talhah, Hamzah and Abu Bakr read it with a kasrah. Al-Zamakhshari said: It has been read: "wa-la tadʿū", from "idda'a al-qawm" and "tada'aw" when they claim (idda'aw), like your saying: "irtamaw al-ṣayd" and "taramaw" (they shot at the game). End of quote. The recitation is without "lā", and it should have been that he would come with the wording of the recitation and say: "And it has been read: wa-tadʿū" — it is connected to "tahinū" (do not weaken), so it is jussive, and it could be jussive by the implied "in" (inna).

(And you are the superior ones): that is, al-aʿlayūn (the superiors). This sentence is in the circumstantial position (ḥāliyyah), and likewise ﴿وَاللَّهُ مَعَكُمْ﴾ ("and Allah is with you"). ﴿And He will not deprive you﴾: Ibn ʿAbbas said: "He will not wrong you." It was said: "He will not strip you of the reward of your deeds." It was said: "He will not diminish you." Al-Zamakhshari said, and Abu ʿUbayd said: "lan yatirakum" is from "watarta al-rajul", when you kill a slain person for him from a son, a brother, a close relative or kinsman. He said: or you take his wealth. He said: or his property. Its reality is that you make him single out from his relative or his wealth, from "al-watr", which is "the single" (al-fard). So the waste of the doer's work and the nullifying of its reward is compared to the "watr" of the one who takes the blood-revenge, and this is among eloquent speech. From it is the saying of the Prophet, upon him be prayer and peace: "Whoever misses the ʿAsr prayer, it is as if he has been robbed of his family and his property," meaning that he was singled out from them by killing and plunder.

﴿The life of this world is but play and amusement﴾: This is a belittling of the effect of this world, that is, "so do not weaken (p-86) in jihad." He informed about it with that, with regard to what is specific to it of such things. As for what is in it of obedience and the affairs of the Hereafter, it is not included in that.

﴿He will give you your rewards﴾: that is, the reward of your deeds of faith and piety. ﴿And will not ask of you your wealth﴾. Sufyan ibn ʿUyaynah said: that is, much of your wealth; He only asks you for a quarter of a tenth, so be generous of your souls. It was said: there is no need for it, rather He returns the reward of your spending to you. It was said: He only asks you for His wealth, because He is the true owner of it, and He is the Bestower by giving it. It was said: the pronoun in "yas'alukum" refers to the Messenger, meaning He does not ask you for a wage for conveying the message, as He said: ﴿Say: I do not ask you for any reward for it, and I am not of those who impose themselves﴾ [Sad 86].

(If He should ask it of you all and press you): that is, he insists in urging.

﴿You would be stingy and He would bring forth your resentments﴾: that is, you would revile the Messenger, your hearts would be constricted likewise, and you would conceal a grudge that would take your wealth. The majority read ﴿ويُخْرِجْ أضْغانَكُمْ﴾ in the jussive, as the answer to the condition, and the verb is attributed to Allah, or to the Messenger, or to stinginess. ʿAbd al-Warith, from Abu ʿAmr, read "wa-yukhriju" with a raf (nominative) as a resumptive sentence, meaning "and He brings forth." Abu Hatim related it from ʿIsa. In al-Lawamih, from ʿAbd al-Warith, from Abu ʿAmr: "wa-takhruju" with a tāʾ and a fatḥah on it, with a ḍammah on the rāʾ and the jīm, and "aḍghānukum" in the nominative, meaning "and it comes out" or "your resentments will come out," with the raf governed by its verb. Yaʿqub read "wa-nukhriju" with a nūn, and "aḍghānukum" in the nominative, and this is related from ʿIsa, except that he made the jīm a fatḥah by the implied "an" (that), so the wāw is a conjunction on an implied verbal noun, meaning "He restrains your stinginess and the bringing forth of your resentments." This is what was feared would befall the believers, and it is what Muhammad ibn Maslamah drew near to Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf with, and by it he reached his killing, when he said to him: "This man has burdened us and demanded wealth from us."

(There you are, these are the ones): He repeated "ha" as an emphatic exclamation of attention. This construction was discussed earlier in surah Al ʿImran. Al-Zamakhshari said: "Haʾulaʾ" is a relative pronoun (mawṣūl) in the sense of "alladhīna," whose relative clause is "tud'awna," meaning "you are those who are called," or "you, O addressees, are these described ones." (In the way of Allah): it was said: for fighting, and it was said: the zakat, and the wording is more general.

In these two sentences there is nearness (taqrīb) (p-85) to their notoriety, but He did not specify them by name, out of sparing them and their relatives, and being content with what they displayed of following the Law, even if they concealed the opposite of it.

﴿And you will surely recognize them by the tone of their speech﴾: They used to agree among themselves on expressions that they addressed to the Messenger, whose outward meaning was good while they meant something ugly by them. They also would utter speech that suggested following [the Messenger], while they were contrary to that, like their saying at the time of victory: ﴿Indeed, we were with you﴾ [al-ʿAnkabūt 10], and other such things, like their saying: ﴿If we return to Madinah﴾ [al-Munafiqun 8], and His saying: ﴿Indeed, our houses are exposed﴾ [al-Ahzab 13]. The apparent meaning of "showing" and "recognizing by marks" is the existence of recognition in the future through the tone of speech. The lam in ﴿ولَتَعْرِفَنَّهم﴾ ("and you will surely recognize them") is the lam of the answer to an implied oath (lām jawāb al-qasam al-maḥdhūf).

﴿And Allah knows your deeds﴾: This is a general address that includes the believer and the disbeliever. It has been said that it is addressed to the believers only.

The meaning of ﴿حَتّى نَعْلَمَ المُجاهِدِينَ﴾ is: that We know them as strivers, whose striving has come into existence, and whose reward is connected to what they have earned (?) — and that their "mask" (maskuhum) on which their reward depends. "Guidance became clear" means its existence with the one who calls to it, or it is widespread in every disbeliever. "Guidance became clear" from the standpoint of what it was in itself: these are opinions.

(O you who believe): It was said that it was revealed about the Children of Israel, who embraced Islam and said to the Messenger of Allah: "We have preferred you and come to you with our souls and our families," as if they were conferring a favour by this. From Muqatil: by your disobedience to the Messenger. It was also said: "your deeds" means your charities accompanied by reproach and harm.

﴿And He will not deprive you﴾: Ibn ʿAbbas said: "He will not wrong you." It was said: "He will not strip you of the reward of your deeds." It was said: "He will not diminish you." Al-Zamakhshari said, and Abu ʿUbayd said: "lan yatirakum" is from "watarta al-rajul", when you kill a slain person for him from a son, a brother, a close relative or kinsman. ﴿The life of this world is but play and amusement﴾: This is a belittling of the effect of this world, that is, "so do not weaken (p-86) in jihad." He informed about it with that, with regard to what is specific to it of such things. As for what is in it of obedience and the affairs of the Hereafter, it is not included in that.

﴿He will give you your rewards﴾: that is, the reward of your deeds of faith and piety. ﴿And will not ask of you your wealth﴾. Sufyan ibn ʿUyaynah said: that is, much of your wealth; He only asks you for a quarter of a tenth, so be generous of your souls. It was said: there is no need for it, rather He returns the reward of your spending to you. On this view, ﴿ولا تُبْطِلُوا أعْمالَكُمْ﴾ ("do not nullify your deeds") means by conferring favour through Islam. From Ibn ʿAbbas: by showing off and seeking reputation. From him also: by associating partners with Allah and hypocrisy. From Hudhayfah: by major sins. It was said: by self-admiration (ʿujb), for it consumes good deeds as fire consumes firewood. From Muqatil: by your disobedience to the Messenger. It was also said: "your deeds" means your charities accompanied by reproach and harm.

(And died while they were disbelievers): It is general regarding what necessitates the absence of forgiveness, which is their death upon disbelief. It was said: they are the people of the well (ahl al-qalīb). It was said: it was revealed on account of ʿAdi ibn Hatim, may Allah be pleased with him, who asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about his father. He said: "He had acts of righteousness; so what is his state?" He said: "In the Fire." ʿAdi wept and turned away, and [the Prophet] called him back and said to him: "My father and your father and the father of Ibrahim, the Friend of the Most Merciful, are in the Fire." Then this was revealed.

Al-Sulami read it with a shaddah on the dāl, meaning "that you become weak" (tafturū). The majority read ﴿إلى السَّلْمِ﴾ with a fatḥah on the sīn, while al-Hasan, Abu Rajaʾ, al-Aʿmash, ʿIsa, Talhah, Hamzah and Abu Bakr read it with a kasrah. The discussion of "al-salm" (peace) has already occurred in al-Baqarah in His saying: ﴿Enter into peace completely﴾ [al-Baqarah 208]. Al-Zamakhshari said: It has been read: "wa-la tadʿū", from "idda'a al-qawm" and "tada'aw" when they claim (idda'aw), like your saying: "irtamaw al-ṣayd" and "taramaw" (they shot at the game). End of quote. Al-Zamakhshari said, and Abu ʿUbayd said: "lan yatirakum" is from "watarta al-rajul", when you kill a slain person for him from a son, a brother, a close relative or kinsman. From it is the saying of the Prophet, upon him be prayer and peace: "Whoever misses the ʿAsr prayer, it is as if he has been robbed of his family and his property," meaning that he was singled out from them by killing and plunder.

﴿The life of this world is but play and amusement﴾: This is a belittling of the effect of this world, that is, "so do not weaken (p-86) in jihad." He informed about it with that, with regard to what is specific to it of such things. As for what is in it of obedience and the affairs of the Hereafter, it is not included in that.

﴿He will give you your rewards﴾: that is, the reward of your deeds of faith and piety. ﴿And will not ask of you your wealth﴾. Sufyan ibn ʿUyaynah said: that is, much of your wealth; He only asks you for a quarter of a tenth, so be generous of your souls. It was said: there is no need for it, rather He returns the reward of your spending to you. It was said: He only asks you for His wealth, because He is the true owner of it, and He is the Bestower by giving it. In these two sentences there is nearness (taqrīb) (p-85) to their notoriety, but He did not specify them by name, out of sparing them and their relatives, and being content with what they displayed of following the Law, even if they concealed the opposite of it.

﴿And you will surely recognize them by the tone of their speech﴾: They used to agree among themselves on expressions that they addressed to the Messenger, whose outward meaning was good while they meant something ugly by them. They also would utter speech that suggested following [the Messenger], while they were contrary to that, like their saying at the time of victory: ﴿Indeed, we were with you﴾ [al-ʿAnkabūt 10], and other such things, like their saying: ﴿If we return to Madinah﴾ [al-Munafiqun 8], and His saying: ﴿Indeed, our houses are exposed﴾ [al-Ahzab 13]. The apparent meaning of "showing" and "recognizing by marks" is the existence of recognition in the future through the tone of speech. The lam in ﴿ولَتَعْرِفَنَّهم﴾ ("and you will surely recognize them") is the lam of the answer to an implied oath (lām jawāb al-qasam al-maḥdhūf).

﴿And Allah knows your deeds﴾: This is a general address that includes the believer and the disbeliever. It has been said that it is addressed to the believers only.

The majority (al-Jumhur) read ﴿ولَنَبْلُوَنَّكم حَتّى نَعْلَمَ المُجاهِدِينَ مِنكُمْ﴾ and ﴿ونَبْلُوَ﴾ with the nūn and the wāw. Abu Bakr read them with the yā' in all of these places. Uways read ﴿ونَبْلَوْا﴾ with a sukūn on the wāw and with the nūn. Al-A'mash read them with a sukūn on it and with the yā'. This is by way of independent sentences (qaṭʿ), to inform that His testing is continuous. The meaning of ﴿حَتّى نَعْلَمَ المُجاهِدِينَ﴾ is: that We know them as strivers, whose striving has come into existence, and whose reward is connected to what they have earned (?) — and that their "mask" (maskuhum) on which their reward depends. ("Those who disbelieved") refers to some people of the Children of Israel. The "clarity of their guidance" means their recognition of the Messenger from the Torah. Or they are hypocrites, as if faith had entered their hearts and then they became hypocrites. "Those who were fed" are the people of Badr's provisions. "Guidance became clear" means its existence with the one who calls to it, or it is widespread in every disbeliever. "Guidance became clear" from the standpoint of what it was in itself: these are opinions.

﴿And He will make their deeds fruitless﴾: that is, the deeds by which they hoped for benefit, and "their deeds" by which they plotted against the Messenger and the religion of Islam.

(O you who believe): It was said that it was revealed about the Children of Israel, who embraced Islam and said to the Messenger of Allah: "We have preferred you and come to you with our souls and our families," as if they were conferring a favour by this. So this verse was revealed about them. And His saying: ﴿They consider it a favour to you that they have embraced Islam﴾ [al-Hujurat 17]. On this view, ﴿ولا تُبْطِلُوا أعْمالَكُمْ﴾ ("do not nullify your deeds") means by conferring favour through Islam. From Ibn ʿAbbas: by showing off and seeking reputation. From him also: by associating partners with Allah and hypocrisy. From Hudhayfah: by major sins. It was said: by self-admiration (ʿujb), for it consumes good deeds as fire consumes firewood. From Muqatil: by your disobedience to the Messenger. It was also said: "your deeds" means your charities accompanied by reproach and harm.

(And died while they were disbelievers): It is general regarding what necessitates the absence of forgiveness, which is their death upon disbelief. It was said: they are the people of the well (ahl al-qalīb). It was said: it was revealed on account of ʿAdi ibn Hatim, may Allah be pleased with him, who asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about his father. He said: "He had acts of righteousness; so what is his state?" He said: "In the Fire." ʿAdi wept and turned away, and [the Prophet] called him back and said to him: "My father and your father and the father of Ibrahim, the Friend of the Most Merciful, are in the Fire." Then this was revealed.

﴿So do not weaken and call to peace﴾: and it is reconciliation (ṣulḥ). The majority read ﴿وتَدْعُوا﴾ as the present tense of "daʿā". Al-Sulami read it with a shaddah on the dāl, meaning "that you become weak" (tafturū). The majority read ﴿إلى السَّلْمِ﴾ with a fatḥah on the sīn, while al-Hasan, Abu Rajaʾ, al-Aʿmash, ʿIsa, Talhah, Hamzah and Abu Bakr read it with a kasrah. The discussion of "al-salm" (peace) has already occurred in al-Baqarah in His saying: ﴿Enter into peace completely﴾ [al-Baqarah 208]. Al-Zamakhshari said: It has been read: "wa-la tadʿū", from "idda'a al-qawm" and "tada'aw" when they claim (idda'aw), like your saying: "irtamaw al-ṣayd" and "taramaw" (they shot at the game). End of quote. The recitation is without "lā", and it should have been that he would come with the wording of the recitation and say: "And it has been read: wa-tadʿū" — it is connected to "tahinū" (do not weaken), so it is jussive, and it could be jussive by the implied "in" (inna).

(And you are the superior ones): that is, al-aʿlayūn (the superiors). This sentence is in the circumstantial position (ḥāliyyah), and likewise ﴿وَاللَّهُ مَعَكُمْ﴾ ("and Allah is with you"). It is also permissible that both be resumptive sentences (jumlatay istiʾnāf), in which He first informed by His saying: "you are the superior ones", and this is information of an unseen matter brought into existence, then He ascended to a rank higher than the one before it, which is that Allah the Exalted is with them.

﴿And He will not deprive you﴾: Ibn ʿAbbas said: "He will not wrong you." It was said: "He will not strip you of the reward of your deeds." It was said: "He will not diminish you." Al-Zamakhshari said, and Abu ʿUbayd said: "lan yatirakum" is from "watarta al-rajul", when you kill a slain person for him from a son, a brother, a close relative or kinsman. He said: or you take his wealth. He said: or his property. Its reality is that you make him single out from his relative or his wealth, from "al-watr", which is "the single" (al-fard). So the waste of the doer's work and the nullifying of its reward is compared to the "watr" of the one who takes the blood-revenge, and this is among eloquent speech. From it is the saying of the Prophet, upon him be prayer and peace: "Whoever misses the ʿAsr prayer, it is as if he has been robbed of his family and his property," meaning that he was singled out from them by killing and plunder.

﴿The life of this world is but play and amusement﴾: This is a belittling of the effect of this world, that is, "so do not weaken (p-86) in jihad." He informed about it with that, with regard to what is specific to it of such things. As for what is in it of obedience and the affairs of the Hereafter, it is not included in that.

﴿He will give you your rewards﴾: that is, the reward of your deeds of faith and piety. ﴿And will not ask of you your wealth﴾. Sufyan ibn ʿUyaynah said: that is, much of your wealth; He only asks you for a quarter of a tenth, so be generous of your souls. It was said: there is no need for it, rather He returns the reward of your spending to you. It was said: He only asks you for His wealth, because He is the true owner of it, and He is the Bestower by giving it. It was said: the pronoun in "yas'alukum" refers to the Messenger, meaning He does not ask you for a wage for conveying the message, as He said: ﴿Say: I do not ask you for any reward for it, and I am not of those who impose themselves﴾ [Sad 86].

(If He should ask it of you all and press you): that is, he insists in urging.

﴿You would be stingy and He would bring forth your resentments﴾: that is, you would revile the Messenger, your hearts would be constricted likewise, and you would conceal a grudge that would take your wealth. The majority read ﴿ويُخْرِجْ أضْغانَكُمْ﴾ in the jussive, as the answer to the condition, and the verb is attributed to Allah, or to the Messenger, or to stinginess. ʿAbd al-Warith, from Abu ʿAmr, read "wa-yukhriju" with a raf (nominative) as a resumptive sentence, meaning "and He brings forth." Abu Hatim related it from ʿIsa. In al-Lawamih, from ʿAbd al-Warith, from Abu ʿAmr: "wa-takhruju" with a tāʾ and a fatḥah on it, with a ḍammah on the rāʾ and the jīm, and "aḍghānukum" in the nominative, meaning "and it comes out" or "your resentments will come out," with the raf governed by its verb. Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid, Ibn Sirin, Ibn Muhaysin, Ayyub ibn al-Mutawakkil and al-Yamani read "wa-takhruju," with a feminine tāʾ and a fatḥah, and "aḍghānukum" is raised by it. Yaʿqub read "wa-nukhriju" with a nūn, and "aḍghānukum" in the nominative, and this is related from ʿIsa, except that he made the jīm a fatḥah by the implied "an" (that), so the wāw is a conjunction on an implied verbal noun, meaning "He restrains your stinginess and the bringing forth of your resentments." This is what was feared would befall the believers, and it is what Muhammad ibn Maslamah drew near to Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf with, and by it he reached his killing, when he said to him: "This man has burdened us and demanded wealth from us."

(There you are, these are the ones): He repeated "ha" as an emphatic exclamation of attention. This construction was discussed earlier in surah Al ʿImran. Al-Zamakhshari said: "Haʾulaʾ" is a relative pronoun (mawṣūl) in the sense of "alladhīna," whose relative clause is "tud'awna," meaning "you are those who are called," or "you, O addressees, are these described ones." Then he resumed describing them, as if they had said: "What is our description?" and it was said: "You are called to spend in the way of Allah." End of quote. The relative pronoun "haʾulaʾ" when preceded by an interrogative "mā" is agreed upon, or by the interrogative "man" according to a difference of opinion. (In the way of Allah): it was said: for fighting, and it was said: the zakat, and the wording is more general.

﴿And among you are some who are stingy﴾: that is, with charity and what Allah has made obligatory upon him. ﴿And whoever is stingy is only stingy against himself﴾: that is, his harm does not pass to others. The verb "bakhila" is transitive with "ʿalā" and with "ʿan." It is said: "bakhiltu ʿalayhi" and "ʿanhu," and "ṣallaytu ʿalayhi" and "ʿanhu." It seems that when they are transitive with "ʿan," they imply the meaning of withholding, as if it were said: "I withheld from him by stinginess."

﴿And Allah is the Free of need and you are the needy﴾: that is, the Free of need absolutely, since needs are impossible for Him. And you are the needy absolutely, due to your need for what you require in this world and for the reward in the Hereafter. (And if you turn away): it is a conjunction on "(and if you believe and fear Allah)," that is, "and if you turn away," that is, from faith and piety.

﴿He will replace you with another people﴾: that is, He will create a people other than you who are eager for faith and piety, not turning away from them, as He said: "and bring a new creation." The identification of those people, and that they are the Ansar, or the Successors (al-Tabiʿun), or the people of Yemen, or Kindah and al-Nakhaʿ, or the non-Arabs, or Persia and the Romans, or the angels, are opinions. The address is to the Quraysh, or to the people of Madinah, are two views. Abu Hurayrah related that "he, upon him be prayer and peace, was asked about this, and Salman was at his side, so he placed his hand on his thigh and said: 'This one and his people; by Him in whose hand is my soul, if faith were suspended at the Pleiades, men from Persia would reach it.'" If this hadith is authentic, then it is necessary to refer the identification of what is left vague in His saying ("another people") to the identification by the Messenger.

﴿Then they will not be like you﴾: that is, in opposition, turning away, and stinginess.
